messages:
Evelyn Tran: heads up — running into edgecases with saved queries when users pin per-route vs per-model filters. current console UI treats them the same which is confusing.
Ravi Patel: can you give an example of the confusing state?
Evelyn Tran: sure. user creates a saved query scoped to Route A but includes a model filter (gpt-open-7b). when they reuse it on Route B the model filter lingers and fails silently (different pinning semantics)
Jordan K: ugh. that explains the 'why my filters changed' tickets yesterday :grimacing:
Priya Singh: quick q — are saved queries currently storing both scope and explicit predicates in the same object? or do we rely on route resolution at render time?
Evelyn Tran: atm we store a single payload: scope: "route" | "model" | "global" + array of predicates. frontend applies predicates as-is. backend doesn't validate compatibility.
Ravi Patel: we should validate at save time and add a compatibility hint when applying. e.g., if model in predicates isn't available for target route, show a banner and offer a fallback.
Jordan K: +1. also think about an explicit "pinnedTo" metadata so UI can show "this saved view is pinned to Route A (model filters may not apply)".
Priya Singh: UX question: should the save dialog force you to pick scope (Route / Model / Global)? or default to context but let you opt out?
Evelyn Tran: default to context (the route you're on) but show a small toggle: "Make this view model-aware" with an info tooltip. keep it non-blocking.
Ravi Patel: backend API change needed: add `scope` and `pinned_resource` fields. example contract:
```json
{
  "name": "High RTs - Route A",
  "scope": "route",
  "pinned_resource": { "type": "route", "id": "route_abc123" },
  "predicates": ["latency > 300", "model == 'gpt-open-7b'"],
  "owner": "team-observability"
}
```
Evelyn Tran: exactly. and when applying a saved query we run a compatibility check server-side and return `compatibility: ["ok" | "model_mismatch" | "route_missing_predicate"]` so UI can surface guidance.
ops-bot: reminder: deploy window for console-api v2 is Thu 03:00 UTC — if this touches API contract, we need to schedule migration.
Jordan K: if we add validation we should also add migration path for existing saved queries. maybe a nightly job that flags incompatible ones and annotates them with `legacy_compat`.
Priya Singh: agreed. can we add a lightweight telemetry event when a saved query is applied and compatibility isn't ok? want to measure how often users hit the model mismatch.
Ravi Patel: yes — emit `saved_query.apply` with tags { scope, compatibility, route, model_list } — make sample rate 1% initially.
Evelyn Tran: TODOs: 1) API change PR (backend) 2) migration job proposal (data) 3) small UX tweak for save dialog + compatibility banner (frontend). I'll create tickets and link here.
Jordan K: ping me on the API PR, I can review the compatibility enum naming.
Priya Singh: i'll draft the telemetry schema and propose event fields.
Ravi Patel: I'll prototype the server-side compatibility checks and a small endpoint `/saved_queries/:id/validate?target_route=...` for the UI to call.
Evelyn Tran: awesome, thanks all :thumbsup:
